Excited to share that I’ve officially joined Harmonic Security as their new Growth and Demand Gen Marketing Manager! The problem Harmonic is solving is one I genuinely believe matters: enabling the safe use of AI. As AI becomes embedded in how every team works, organizations are facing a real question: how do you let your people benefit from these tools without putting sensitive data at risk? Harmonic’s answer is elegant. Rather than simply blocking AI tools, Harmonic gives security teams full visibility into how AI is being used across their organization, detects sensitive data in real time using their own small language models, and coaches employees toward secure behavior at the exact moment it matters. I couldn’t be more proud to join this team. Getting to know Ana Corio and Michael Marriott throughout the process, and being able to work alongside my good friend Jackson Harrower, made this decision incredibly easy. The depth of thinking and the genuine excitement about what they’re building stood out from the very first conversation. I can’t wait to get to work.

**Tyler Chonoles**: Growth and Demand Gen Marketing Manager at Harmonic Security for 2 months with 7 years 1 month of total professional experience. **Tyler Chonoles**: Growth and Demand Gen Marketing Manager at Harmonic Security for 2 months with 7 years 1 month of total professional experience. Previous roles include Programmatic Trading Specialist at The Trade Desk, Business Intelligence Architect at GRAIN Group, and Senior Analyst, Data Analytics at Horizon Media. Based in New York City Metropolitan Area [US].

---

Most organizations can tell you which AI tools their teams are using. Very few can tell you what work is actually getting done inside them.

That gap is what AI Usage Explorer is built to close! 🚀

Today [Harmonic Security](https://linkedin.com/company/harmonic-security) launched Usage Intelligence - and AI Usage Explorer is the first place you'll see it in the portal. Instead of raw interaction counts, you get a real picture of what your organization is using AI for. Not "the sales team used ChatGPT 300 times" - but "the sales team is drafting cold outreach emails for enterprise prospects, and usage is growing week over week."

Use cases are discovered from your actual data. No predefined categories. Every organization's AI map looks different - because it is.

Security teams finally have something to bring to the AI governance conversation that isn't just a list of policy violations.

BRUNSWICK, Maine - The Bowdoin College men's golf team placed ninth at its season-opening Bowdoin Invitational this weekend at the Brunswick Golf Club. The Polar Bears recorded a team total of 664 (+88) as a team. St. Anselm took the crown with a two-day score of 603 (+27). - Liam Farley(170) finished in a tie for 37th in his first collegiate tournament, followed by Jackson Harrower(171) in 40th, and Tyler Chonoles and Eric Giesler in a tie for 42nd (172).
- Bowdoin's top performer was Thomas Dunleavy, who finished in eighth place individually (+12, 156), just 12 strokes off the winning score.
